about: recon's layers, checked by tests/test_layering.py on every test run with the shared checker (components/capabilities/_testing/layers.py), which reads a map as slick crafting-aces' layer-check.py does, so the same file runs under that script too. Two layers (recon 0.18, step M3): the collect core (src/recon/core: one act fetched, captured, converted, normalized and landed with its checkpoint; the plan of one act; query) and the observe layer (src/recon/observe: span planning, schedules, windows over time, follow, change derivation after the seal, subscriptions, delivery, status). The core never imports the observe layer; the observe layer reaches the core only through recon.core's __all__ (an allowance here is a prefix, so test_layering holds every observe file to that __all__ by name). Each layer keeps its ports in its domain/ beside its model. 'why' keys are read by neither checker.
scan_why: Every Python file in the package. Tests are out of scan: a test reaches adapters by design.

why.stdlib: recon's PURE_STDLIB (tests/test_layering.py): pathlib names a location and datetime is the type the clock port returns; touching the filesystem or reading the clock through them is caught by test_layering's effect scan
why.shlex: splitting a command line given as a string into words, to find the packages a scheduled command fetches (domain/schedule.py's unpinned); no stream is handed it, so it reads no file
why.fnmatch: fnmatchcase alone, a glob matched against a string (a subscription's match:, domain/subscriptions.py), as the capture collector's match: is; it reads no file
why.threading: TIMEOUT_MAX alone, the longest wait the platform's timers take, which the plan holds a source's timeout and rate to (domain/clock.py); the domain starts no thread (test_layering's LAYER_STDLIB). Accepted: owner ruling 2026-10-22
why.pydantic: every published document and config model is a pydantic model
why.forbid: the adapters' technologies, YAML, and the builtin open, which no import shows

why.hashlib, json: the config's sha256 in the archive's meta, a hook payload's body, and a stream's records as the buffer holds them (test_layering's LAYER_STDLIB)
why.hmac: compare_digest alone: a change cursor's signature compared in constant time (application/subscriptions.py)
why.threading: a stream's pump and ticker threads and its bounded buffer (application/stream.py), where ruling B1 puts them; every wait for time goes through the clock port (test_layering's LAYER_STDLIB)
why.recon.core.domain, recon.core.applicatio: the core's services run one act over its ports, in its domain's types

why.recon.core: the core's public names, re-exported from its domain and application: what the observe layer and any outside driver may use

why.html, re, fnmatch: a projected scheduler file's escaping, a delivery's text cleaned of escapes, a match: glob: string work alone
why.recon.core: the core's public names alone (recon.core.__all__, held by test_layering): the config a schedule, a subscription or a range is read from
why.forbid: the adapters' technologies, YAML, and the builtin open, which no import shows

why.hmac: compare_digest alone: a change cursor's signature compared in constant time (application/subscriptions.py)

why.nothing: the observe layer's package marker; its services are reached through the composition root

why.*: body parsing (xmltodict, lazily), the distribution's version for the User-Agent, how a request to an HTTP source is addressed and carries its credential (shared by api and sse), the modes every file and directory of a mission is made with (ruling A2: shared by the stores and the cli collector's capture), where every source kind's credential comes from (a variable, a file, a helper's headers: shared by api, sse and mcp, ruling A1), the flock a store holds on a mission's file and the bounded log it appends to (shared by the archive, schedule and subscription stores), and where a mission's files are (mission_layout: the one map of a mission's name, an archive's reference and a stream's name to directories, shared by every file store and the composition root)
why.recon.core.domain: the errors a bad body raises; these helpers hold no port and reach no adapter
why.recon.adapters._out.credentials: http_source sends the credential the shared resolver gives
why.recon.adapters._out.private_files: a lock file and a log are made private, as every file of a mission is

why.*: one technology, the local filesystem, and YAML for the archive's meta and the mission's config
why.mission_layout: where a mission's files are: the one map every file store shares
why.capture_files, event_log: the archive store composes the archive's capture log and event log, and the mission store reuses the capture log for the mission's external log: one technology composing its own files
why.private_files: every file and directory a store makes is made private (ruling A2)
why.file_locks: the writer locks a store holds, and the bounded logs it appends to

why.*: each collector type's own technology: a child process for cli, the MCP client (fastmcp, the mcp SDK, jsonschema) for mcp, the local filesystem for tail, nothing beyond the requester port for api, web and sse
why.parsing, user_agent, http_source, privat: the shared helpers (private_files: the cli collector tees its stdout into the archive's capture; credentials: every source kind's credential reference, ruling A1)
why.capture_files: the capture collector reads the capture format through its one reader, so no second parser of the format exists

why.*: the operating system's schedulers, each by its own command run as an argument list (launchctl, systemctl --user, crontab), and the mission's install record as JSON
why.mission_layout: the install record and the tick log are kept in the mission's directory, found through the one map of it
why.private_files: a projected file and the install record are written readable by their owner alone, as every file of a mission is (ruling A2)
why.file_locks: the tick log is the bounded log the stores share

why.recon.core.domain only: which files make an archive is the archive adapter's secret; the query reads the tables the adapter it is built with names (its TableFiles protocol, met structurally), never the layout, and imports no other adapter
why.private_files: the large join's directory under the mission is made private, as every directory of a mission is (ruling A2; round-4 review F7)

why.*: one technology each behind one port: httpx2 and tenacity (Requester), markitdown (DocumentConverter), OpenTelemetry (EventSink), the system clock (Clock), a child process given a delivery on its standard input (Deliverer)
why.recon.core.domain only: an adapter reaches the port it implements, and no other adapter

why.recon: a driving adapter reaches recon through 'import recon' alone. The entry admits every recon.* path, since an allowance is a prefix; test_layering holds every file under adapters/_in to recon.__all__

why.matrix: the one module of recon that names matrix: its registry, its errors (single_importer below)
why.recon.core.domain: the descriptors a point's entries build, and the errors a refusal is said as
why.recon.composition: recon's built-ins, which only the composition root names, registered at recon's points

why.*, recon: the composition root: the one file that chooses adapters (test_layering holds this too)

why.recon.composition, recon.core.domain: the library API names the root and the core's documents and errors, never an adapter or a service
why.*: importlib for the version and the packaged skill files
why.recon._matrix: the type of an extension given to recon.open (Register), named for the type checker alone

why.nothing: empty package markers for importlib.resources (the skill text, the templates)

single_importer_why: one file per technology, each behind one port; the MCP client is the mcp collector's alone, and it reaches httpx2 only through the SDK's own client. YAML is two files by design, the archive store writing the archive's meta and the mission store reading the mission's config, so it is confined to the file store by 'forbid' in every other layer rather than by a single_importer rule; matrix is named by recon/_matrix.py alone, so a move of the harness contract to slick changes one module (owner ruling, REQ §2; RUBRIC H6)
